assign.name: Applied Learning Product 1
assign.intro:
Applied Learning Product 1: Observation of child-to-child interactions – regarding social and emotional skills

This week you are asked to observe a few minutes of child-to-child interactions (not during teacher-led sessions).

Targeted Outcome(s):

  • List specific social and emotional skills appropriate for 3-4-year-old children
  • Implement specific teaching/learning strategies to support the development of social and emotional skills in young children. 

Overview:

In this activity, the participants will observe 2 separate child-to-child interactions and write brief notes about what occurred.  Two brief descriptions of children using (or not using) social and emotional skills will be posted to the Moodle site.  During subsequent class discussions, the participants will relate the interactions to social and emotional skill development.  The participants will identify supportive adult responses to the examples of children’s interactions. 

Instructions:

Briefly describe 2 interactions (with different children, or at other times).  Post these two descriptions. 

Please be prepared to share what you observed about children’s social and emotional skills during the next Synchronous Session (see guiding questions below).  

    • What social skills did you observe children using?
    • What social skills did you observe children needing support to learn?
    • What emotional skills did you observe children using?
    • What emotional skills did you observe children needing support to learn?

1.Lacing the beads:

 children were given  beads and they were allowed to place the amount they wanted in the plate that was handed to them.

 Communication skills :

Children spoke about the colors that was chosen  .Tina  and Joe  sitting next to each other spoke of their favorite color as they place the beads on the lace .

The children were  patient and focused as they try to get the lace into the hole of each bead .

They also  raced with each other. Joe  shouted" I'm going to win". As the competition continues between the two children,  Tina did not finish first she was a bit upset and was saying" I'm not playing with you."

Joe answered "I will let you win the next time ok" , let's do it again . "No am not playing , said Tina with a sad face.

Touching her hand Joe said "go  first I will let you win" Tina was excited as she started to lace the beads. They both laughed and tackle the beads again. A short while after Tina said to "Joe but you have more, look yours is longer"

Tina started saying " not fare as she rest her item on the table and cross her hands over her chest with an angry facial expression.

-After observing for a while I  intervened and  explained to the children that it is ok to be competitive sometimes, it's ok for someone to win in something they are good at .

I also told them that anyone can be a winner .and that there are other things that you might be better at that Joe. I also gave the example of being competitive for our  sports meet ,we just have to work hard and deligent so we an win .

Tina needed the support with empathy.understanding that it's ok for someone else to win .

         Skills learnt 

Fine motor skills: manipulating the lace and the beads , which helps with hand / eye co ordination 

They were concentrating - focusing on the task at hand , which inturn improves their attention span 

Children were able to follow instructions - being creative choosing their own colors 

Children also develop social emotion skills as they express how they feel.

2. Dramatic play : using kitchen set

Social skills observed 

  • there was alot of communication, role playing and discussing what they where cooking .
  • Co operation - working together in an imaginary pretend kitchen , they learn team work as they share the utensils 
  • They took on different roles as they play with each other.
  • Conflict resolution - when the disagreed on something, when  Tina wanted the stove but another child was using it ,she ask James to take it for her .James then pulled it from Seara , but when Seara started to cry Tina gave it back to her,and  asked her to stop crying.

Imaginative play - the children cooking and engaging with each other at the setting express themselves socially and emotionally, they never called on me to resolve their issues .

There was  hardly any need for caregiver to intervene, since children were able to solve their problems on their own.

They learnt some vital emotional skills 

Self regulation - they waited for their turn to use some of the utensils and even asked for it politely.

They were able to express their feelings during cooking, they were very excited as they took the plates  to  dish out the pretend food. Children learn to share with each other .

As children  are engaged in this type of play it help them boost up their self confidence and self esteem. They initiated that and showed that they were incharge of what was being done.

  • there was also self awareness: paid attention to the feelings of others.

There was hardly any need for teacher's intervention as children quickly learn to say I'm sorry or when a friend cry if something was taken away , they were quick to give it back .

First interaction.

During freeplay i noticed a child sitting at the table on her own while the other children played together. I walked up to her and asked why she was sitting on her own. She said that the other girls did not want her to play with them. I then called over the girls and asked why she was not allowed to play. The girls indicated to me that she never came up to them to ask to play. Realising what was said by the other children she then asked them to play and they agreed. I praised her for realising her error and making the situation better for herself.  

Second interaction. 

There is a student who is an only child in his family and has no younger family members to interact with. when he comes to school he is unsure of how to interact with the other children. I would observe him circling them first then maybe if they are building a tower and he would knock it down. The children would either complain about him or ask him to stop. Sometimes when i would intervene he would shut down and not answer any questions, until i would ask the other children how do they feel about what he did and to explain to him how we make friends and how to treat a friend. We also had a lesson on friendship and modeled positive behaviour of friendship.

One mornings nick enters play did not greet anyone ,Rita call and said "Nick you did not say good morning.

Interaction #1. Taking turns on the slide.

Lean and Bella were at the playground. Bella climbs the slide first and slides down. Lean excitedly climbs up but doesn't wait for Bella to move away before going down. She bumps into Bella at the bottom and gets upset. “Move!” Yelled Lean as she moved pass Bella. Bella began to cry and said that Lean pushed her. Teacher reminds them to be nice to each other and take turns sliding. They hug, say sorry and go back to sliding and having fun. 

Social/ Emotional skills used: 

Taking turns- Lean and Bella were nice to each other and to turns sliding.

Bella showed that she was upset when Bella bumped into her. 

Expressing feelings- saying sorry 

Social/ Emotional Skills children need support to learn:

Patience- Bella did not wait for Lean to move before sliding.

Awareness of safety- Bella needs to understand the importance of being safe. Bumping into someone could hurt them. 

Interaction #2. Playtime

Patrice and Shaun are playing with blocks. patrice builds a tower, while Shaun gathers blocks to make a house. Shaun notices that Patrice has many blocks and asks if he can have some. Patrice gives him a few. He takes them and start to build but realizes he needs more blocks. Instead of asking, Shaun grabs some from Patrice's pile. She gets upset and knocks his house over. She takes back her blocks and tell him to ask. Shaun sits in silence for a minute and then ask Patrice if he could have more blocks. 

Social/ Emotional skills used:

 Asking politely/ sharing resources- Shaun asks for the blocks and Patrice shared, showing generosity. 

Communication- Shaun expressed his need for blocks. 

Social/ Emotional skills children need support to learn: 

Respecting personal space and belongings- Shaun took more blocks without asking and upsets Patrice. 

Managing Frustration/Emotions- Patrice reacts by knocking Shaun's house down instead of using her words.
